subject: Dedicated capacity MAP — Align owners, throughput targets, and eval plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Tran <alyssa.tran@aurorahealth.ai>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@aurorahealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity MAP — Align owners, throughput targets, and eval plan

Hi Alyssa / Tom,

Thanks again for the productive demo yesterday. As discussed, I wanted to start a concise mutual action plan (MAP) thread to align owners, capacity targets, and the evaluation milestones that will drive our close timeline for Aurora Health's dedicated GPU pool.

Attached is a draft MAP (MAP_v1.0.xlsx) that I populated with recommended milestones. High-level ask: can your team confirm owners and feasibility of the throughput targets by EOD Tuesday 4/5? If we lock owners and targets this week, we can schedule a 2-week evaluation window and aim for a mid-May go/no-go decision.

Key items in the draft:
- Target throughput: 300 rps at 4-token average latency < 120ms (p99) for inference during peak hours — preliminary estimate
- Evaluation plan: 2-week run with a synthetic traffic profile + 3 customer-critical prompt families (we'll share eval harness)
- Deliverables: capacity runbook, access plan (VPC peering or private endpoint), preliminary SLA language (SLA_draft.pdf)

Proposed owners (please adjust):
- Aurora product lead: Alyssa Tran
- Aurora procurement: Procurement team (cc'd)
- Redwood delivery lead: Vivek Kulkarni
- Redwood infra/engineering: Markus Klein (runtime tuning)
- Redwood solutions/benchmarks: Rishi Malhotra
- Customer success & rollout: Monica Patel

Next steps:
1) Confirm owners & throughput targets (due 4/05)
2) Redwood to deliver eval harness and reqs (due 4/06)
3) 2-week evaluation window (w/c 4/11)
4) Mid-May decision meeting (target 5/13)

If you prefer, we can split the evaluation into a low-latency short-run and a sustained throughput run — happy to model both.

Attachments: MAP_v1.0.xlsx, SLA_draft.pdf

Thanks,

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182
Redwood Inference
From: Alyssa Tran <alyssa.tran@aurorahealth.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@aurorahealth.ai>, Procurement <procurement@aurorahealth.ai>
Date: 2027-04-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity MAP — Align owners, throughput targets, and eval plan

Thanks Vivek — this is helpful.

Quick notes from our side:
- I'll own product sign-off for the evaluation and coordinate prompt families with our clinical NLP lead.
- Tom (cc'd) will own infrastructure/IT coordination and procurement will shepherd the contract bits.
- Procurement asked if you can share the preliminary SLA as a redline-friendly PDF; the attachment you included looks good as a starting point.

Throughput question: 300 rps seems in the right direction but can you clarify if that assumes batching or not? Our peak is very spiky (short bursts up to ~4k rps for a few minutes). If the MAP can include a burst plan (buffering, autoscale) that would help.

We can confirm owners by Monday 4/04 and Tom will follow up on procurement timelines.

Regards,

Alyssa

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity MAP — Align owners, throughput targets, and eval plan

Couple of technical clarifications to help make the MAP actionable:

1) The 300 rps estimate: is that per model endpoint or aggregated across multiple concurrent endpoints? We should specify per-endpoint sustained rps and an aggregate burst headroom. For example: 300 sustained rps per endpoint, with aggregate burst headroom to 4k for 3-minute windows.

2) Batching: our recommended eval harness will run two modes — no-batching (single-token-per-request latency) and adaptive-batching (to demonstrate cost-performance tradeoffs). Please confirm which mode represents Aurora's production traffic; we'll tune accordingly.

3) KV cache & prompt families: please identify the 3 critical prompt families (example: intake summarization, triage classification, results enrichment). We'll instrument for token distribution.

4) Access: for private deployment we'll need the VPC CIDR ranges and an initial list of test IPs for the first week of evaluation.

I'll prepare an initial throughput_projections.csv and a short eval-run checklist by 4/06.

—Rishi

Thanks Rishi & team — this is exactly the level of detail we need.

- Aurora product lead: Alyssa Tran — confirm prompt families list by 4/06
- Aurora infra lead: Tom Ellis — provide VPC CIDR ranges and test IPs by 4/06
- Aurora procurement: Procurement — confirm PO timeline (Tom to advise)
- Redwood delivery lead: Vivek Kulkarni — deliver eval harness and schedule
- Redwood infra/engineering: Markus Klein — runtime tuning & cluster config
- Redwood benchmarks: Rishi Malhotra — projections & eval checklist (due 4/06)
- Customer success: Monica Patel — post-eval rollout plan

Milestones (updated):
- 4/06: Owners confirmed, throughput targets finalized, and eval artifacts delivered (MAP_v1.1)
- 4/11–4/22: Evaluation window (two modes: latency-focused short bursts; sustained throughput)
- 5/13: Decision meeting — go/no-go and contract finalization

On the burst question: we'll include an autoscale + burst headroom clause in MAP_v1.1. The eval harness will simulate 4k rps 3-minute bursts while monitoring p99 latency and error rates.

Attachments updated: MAP_v1.1.xlsx (I'll upload to the Drive and add link), throughput_projections.csv (draft attached)

Can everyone confirm the 4/06 owner/target deadline? If any conflict, flag now and we'll adjust.

Cheers,

Vivek
